sections.title: The Failure of Traditional Dimensions
lecture_lines: Points, lines, and planes have classic dimensions.
Some shapes defy these simple categories.
Nature hides complexity in infinite detail.
animations: Draw a 1D line segment of length 1 in #FFFFFF.
Transform the segment into 2D square by sweeping the segment.
Use a recursive iteration to show the square's complexity, incorporating the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fern.svg] to demonstrate fractal growth.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Scaling Laws
lecture_lines: Scaling determines how an object fills space.
Line segments scale with the power of one.
Squares scale with the power of two.
animations: Draw a line (N=2, S=2) in #00FFFF, place [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg] nearby and label scaling.
Display square (N=4, S=2) in #00FFFF, place [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tile.svg] nearby, labeling the N=S^D relation.
Animate the exponent D = log(N)/log(S) appearing next to the shapes.

sections.title: Defining the Fractal Dimension (Hausdorff)
lecture_lines: Fractal dimension bridges the gap between integers.
We use logarithms to measure scaling behavior.
Koch snowflakes demonstrate this fractional dimension.
Dimension is a measure of roughness.
animations: Create a central formula text: D = log(N) / log(S) in #FFD700.
Animate log(N) and log(S) components flashing to indicate variable inputs.
Display N=4, S=3 for Koch snowflake in #FFD700 [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/snowflake.svg].
Calculate D ≈ 1.26 as the snowflake emerges [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/snowflake.svg].
Place a green target icon at the D value position.

sections.title: Visualizing Complexity
lecture_lines: Iteration increases the object's perceived density.
Sierpinski triangles leave behind structural voids.
Recursive patterns trap area within limited boundaries.
Increasing iterations reveals the hidden fractal geometry.
Higher dimensions imply more space-filling paths.
animations: Use a recursive function call visual to denote iteration 3.
Overlay a grid over the structure showing consistent scaling.
Add a terminal anchor icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/target.svg] on the final iteration geometry.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Nature's Geometry
lecture_lines: Nature utilizes fractals for efficient surface area.
Bronchial trees maximize gas exchange through complexity.
Dimension helps diagnose health and monitor systems.
animations: Draw a simple tree-like structure representing a lung [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lung.svg] in #7FFF00 at coordinate B2.
Place a formula D=1.5 in the central Row D to balance the scene.
Animate the surface area of the [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lung.svg] expanding, showing the D relationship.
